title: end-to-end-request-telemetry-muxer-and-async-boundary-guard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: multiple SDKs and middleware points are implementing ad-hoc propagation logic which leads to context loss across async boundaries (threadpools, worker queues, HTTP/2 multiplexed streams) and inconsistent sampling decisions. Goal: implement a lightweight 'telemetry muxer' core in the SDKs and a small runtime middleware that centralizes trace/span lifecycle, sampling hints, and a minimal envelope for safe propagation through non-HTTP transports. This should be low-overhead for hot paths and resilient to partial metadata loss.
acceptance_criteria: SDK libraries (python/node/go) expose a TelemetryMuxer API that replaces current per-language context shims and preserves trace id + sampling hint across thread boundaries
Telemetry muxer end-to-end test demonstrates context preserved through: async threadpool tasks, GRPC streaming with multiplexed streams, and worker queue handoff
CPU and allocation overhead for hot-path generation increases < 3% under our synthetic load (p95 request mix) compared to baseline
Automatic binary-header fallback implemented: if full envelope not supported, minimal 3-field header (trace_id, span_id, sampling_hint) is extracted and recovered
Land PRs for python/node/go SDKs and a runtime middleware with docs and rollout plan; integration smoke tests passing in staging
comments: 2025-02-11 Maya Chen - Initial ticket created after spike showed 18% context loss for worker-queue handoffs in microbenchmarks. Proposed approach: muxer core + tiny envelope with idempotent decoding.

2025-02-18 Diego Alvarez - Implemented PoC python muxer in branch feat/telemetry-muxer-py. Early results: context preserved through ThreadPoolExecutor tasks but GRPC streaming required special stream affinity token.
2025-02-20 Priya Nair (PM) - Reviewed. PM concern: rollout must default to passive mode (observe-only) for 2 weeks before full enablement to avoid customer-facing regressions.
2025-02-24 Security review (notes) - Verified that envelope does not carry PII. Recommended KMS tagging for signed tokens in Private deployments. No blocking issues.
2025-02-26 Benchmarks - Node muxer microbench: 1.8% p95 latency increase, allocation delta +2.1% on our baseline traces workload. Actions: tune lazy-initialization to push overhead to cold-path.
2025-02-27 Code review Diego -> ENG - runtime PR has a fallback decoder for partially-mangled headers; added tests for partial frames and stream resets.

2025-03-01 QA - Integration smoke: trace stitching flaky on high concurrency GRPC streams. Root cause: stream affinity token collision when short-lived spans are reused. Mitigation: extend affinity token TTL and include sequence nonce.

2025-03-02 Diego Alvarez - Updated plan: land python SDK + runtime middleware in passive observe mode, monitor trace fidelity metric for 72h, then enable active propagation in node/go and enable default in staging. Follow-ups created for sequence nonce hardening and fuzz testing.
notes: Design trade-offs considered: fullcarrier vs minimal envelope. Chosen: minimal idempotent envelope to reduce header bloat and improve cross-protocol resilience.
Fallback behavior: when envelope missing or corrupted, sampler will attach a new local root but emit an observability event for investigation.
Rollout: feature flag controlled per-tenant with 'observe-only' and 'propagate' modes. Default to observe-only for first release.
Follow-ups: create a dedicated fuzz-test job for header mangling, and an automated alert on >1% trace discontinuity after rollout.
